pages.text: Trustee Payment Disclosure Policy - Internet Society Board of Trustees Trustee Payment Disclosure Policy As adopted by Board Resolution 2026-14 on 10 July 20 26 The Internet Society’s Conflict of Interest Policy and Board and Officer Code of Ethics demonstrate the commitment of the Board of Trustees to observing the highest ethical standards, complying with all applicable laws, and maintaining ISOC’s reputation as a respected corporate citizen. As an additional commitment to transparent governance, members of the board also agree to disclose payments, reimbursements or expense sponsorships (“funding”) from the Internet Society for any activity that is not directly related to attending meetings of the board. Any Trustee receiving such unrelated funding from the Internet Society shall disclose to the Chair of the board, via email, the type of funding (e.g. reimbursement for travel and accommodation to speak at a conference as an ISOC Trustee) and the rationale for funding (e.g. expert knowledge of the conference subject matter) at the time he or she requests funding. The Chair of the board will disclose the funding details to the board. Trustees need not disclose expense sponsorship for activities with nominal value, such as attendance at an ISOC dinner or reception which is co-located with a conference the Trustee is attending at his or her own expense.

TSCA Section 21 Under TSCA section 21, any person may petition EPA to initiate a proceeding for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule or order under: Section 4 -- rules or orders requiring chemical testing; Section 6 -- rules imposing regulatory controls on chemicals; Section 8 -- rules requiring information; or Section 5(e) or (f) -- orders affecting new chemical substances. The petition must be filed in EPA's Office of the Administrator and set forth the facts that are claimed to establish the necessity for the action requested. EPA is required to grant or deny the petition within 90 days from the day the petition is filed with EPA. If EPA grants the petition, EPA must promptly commence an appropriate proceeding. If EPA denies the petition, the reasons for denial must be published in the Federal Register. April 2, 2024 Tuberculosis Information for Emergencies and Disasters What to know Emergencies and disasters can make efforts to help TB patients continue their treatment difficult. TB programs work to ensure that people who are receiving treatment for TB are able to continue their treatment, even during an emergency or disaster. The importance of TB treatment TB programs help patients continue treatment.‎ If you are currently taking treatment for TB and your medical visits have been affected by an emergency or disaster, contact your state or local TB program. State TB Programs It is very important that people who have tuberculosis (TB) disease receive treatment, take the medicine exactly as prescribed by their health care provider, and finish the medicine. If they stop taking the medicine too soon, they can become sick again. If they do not take the medicine correctly, the TB bacteria that are still alive may become resistant to those drugs. United States Department of Transportation In This Section Turbulence: Staying Safe What is Turbulence? Turbulence is air movement that normally cannot be seen and often occurs unexpectedly. It can be created by many different conditions, including atmospheric pressure, jet streams, air around mountains, cold or warm weather fronts or thunderstorms. Turbulence can even occur when the sky appears to be clear. While turbulence is normal and happens often, it can be dangerous. Its bumpy ride can cause passengers who are not wearing their seat belts to be thrown from their seats without warning. But by following the guidelines suggested on this site, you can help keep yourself and your loved ones safe when traveling by air. What should passengers do to avoid injuries? Passengers can prevent injuries from unexpected turbulence by: Keeping their seat belt buckled at all times. FAA regulations require passengers to be seated with their seat belts fastened: When the airplane leaves the gate and as it climbs after takeoff During landing and taxi Whenever the seat belt sign is illuminated during flight Listen to the pilots and flight attendants. Обозначение обособленной велосипедной дорожки: highway=cycleway - основной тег линии, который указывает, что путь предназначен для движения на велосипедах. foot=no - явно запрещает движение пешеходов (если пешеходам запрещено находиться на этой дорожке). Если пешеходы разрешены, но дорожка разделена на зоны, используют foot=yes и segregated=yes/no . Велосипедная дорожка + тротуар: Комбинация тэгов для обозначения пешеходного тротуара, совмещённого с выделенной велосипедной дорожкой, которая конструктивно или визуально отделена от пешеходной зоны: highway=footway - обозначает, что данный объект является обустроенной дорожкой, предназначенной в первую очередь для пешеходов. footway=sidewalk - уточняет тип пешеходной дорожки. Этот тег указывает, что дорожка является тротуаром, то есть идет параллельно автомобильной дороге (обычно повторяя её геометрию). bicycle=designated - указывает на официальный юридический статус для велосипедистов. Это значит, что дорожка специально выделена/предназначена для движения на велосипеде (например, установлен соответствующий знак или нанесена разметка), а не просто «разрешена для транзита». segregated=yes - означает, что потоки пешеходов и велосипедистов разделены. We experience it at every moment. And refining our ability to measure it has had immense impact on our world. Surveyors measure local gravity every time they go out in the field. The scientific field of geodesy, which maps the Earth’s shape and predicts where water will flow and minerals can be found, is built on a foundation of gravity measurements. Accurate measurements of gravity are also key to how the world defines the kilogram, the fundamental unit of mass. Today’s most accurate gravity sensors use lasers and atomic clocks to measure how fast a macroscopic reflective object falls in vacuum. Close Tuwewanzi's Diary Basic Overview of the Dakota/Lakota Language Posted by Tuwewanzi on 12 November 2026 in English . Dakota (instead called Lakota by speakers of that dialect ) is the indigenous language of the Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ (Seven Council Fires) people of North America, consisting of the Bdewaḳaƞṭuƞwaƞ, Waḣpeḳute, Waḣpeṭuƞwaƞ, Sisiṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞ, Ihaƞkṭuƞwaƞna and Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ communities. Most members of these communities will describe themselves as Dakota (or Lakota for the Ṭiṭuƞwaƞ) people. Dakota and Lakota communities can be found in Minnesota, North Dakota, South Dakota, Nebraska, Montana, Manitoba and Saskatchewan. All of these places have a rich geography of names devised by Oc̣eṭi Ṡakowiƞ people in the Dakota/Lakota language, including rivers, lakes, towns, islands, hills and more. People have traveled since the dawn of human history and some areas once had Dakota/Lakota communities that presently do not, and so other areas (such as Wisconsin, Iowa, Wyoming and Ontario) also have locations with names in the language. Historically, there have been far, far more Dakota and Lakota place names than those that survive for us to learn about them in the present. When assigning Dakota and Lakota names to map elements, I am mainly drawing on the (often lifelong) work of others; very few of my changes are based on personal local knowledge. I have focused on sources who are either directly part of, or at least worked closely with, authentic Oc̣eti Ṡakowiƞ communities. This is the language of nations that are alive today, and they have things to say! My major sources include: My mapping work owes an enormous amount to (and sits in the shadow of) the absolutely incredible Maḳoc̣e Waṡte map by Lakota historian Dakota Wind Goodhouse, who drew on a vast range of sources to populate the names of thousands of places. His blog The First Scout is one of the best public history projects you’ll find anywhere, and you should check it out. Sometimes my research has led me to different conclusions on the precise meaning and pronunciation of some place names, and the largest limitation of his map is the one he tells you about right away (it is a Landscape Map and so rarely discusses towns and cities) but this is still the single largest, most thorough map of Lakota/Dakota place names you will find anywhere until such time as I can somehow map twice as much content as I have. pages.text: Tuwewanzi's Diary | Dakota/Lakota Dialects | OpenStreetMap Select Language Loading... Close Tuwewanzi's Diary Dakota/Lakota Dialects Posted by Tuwewanzi on 12 November 2026 in English . Last updated on 17 November 2026. My mapping on OpenStreetMap includes names in both Dakota and Lakota, with ISO codes dak and lkt respectively. This is an unusual approach compared to a lot of other multilingual mapping, so it’s worth explaining in more detail. Dakota and Lakota are two different dialects of the same language (and are two possible names for that language). They are mutually intelligible, and a fluent speaker of one can understand a fluent speaker of the other without difficulty. An analogy might be made to the Spanish spoken in Mexico vs the Spanish spoken in Spain - a speaker of the other dialect will seem to have a strong accent, unusual pronunciation, and some different word choices, but they are still clearly speaking your language . Both dialects are endangered, but there are substantially more Lakota speakers than Dakota speakers and this has been true for a long time. Dakota and Lakota share the vast majority of their vocabulary. Most words that differ between these dialects differ in predictable, formulaic ways that do not represent any difference in meaning (e.g. Oṭuƞwe vs Otȟúŋwahe or Bde vs Ble). The most meaningful differences in Lakota vs Dakota speech emerge in conversational flow, which rarely matters for place names. Close Tuwewanzi's Diary Dakota/Lakota Writing Systems and Orthography Posted by Tuwewanzi on 12 November 2026 in English . The Dakota/Lakota language has been a written language for only the most recent chapters of its history. Writing systems for the language were first devised by 19th-century missionaries who sought to promote literacy as a part of encouraging Dakota people to convert to Christianity. These missionaries, especially Stephen Riggs , developed an alphabet based on the Latin Alphabet to represent the sounds present in the language. All widely used methods for writing the language today are based on Riggs’ system with some degree of variation. There is no single writing system accepted by the vast majority of speaker communities. A variety of systems - or orthographies - exist with varying degrees of popularity, and invididual speakers and teachers often have strong preferences one way or another. Areas of debate include: May an orthography make use of special characters (ŋ, ǧ, ḳ, ú) or should writing be done only with characters that can be written with a standard English keyboard? The language contains vowels (a, i, u) that may be nasalized or not, depending on context; should the orthography note the difference? The language contains consonants (z, c, p, t, k, s) that may be aspirated for a harder sound or unaspirated; should the orthography note the difference? pages.description: Long thought to have been looted from northern England by Scottish tribes, the larger-than-life leg may have actually been displayed in Roman Scotland, before it was carefully dismantled and buried by retreating forces
pages.text: Two Centuries After This Bronze Leg Emerged From a Scottish Bog, Archaeologists Believe It May Have Belonged to a Towering Statue of a Roman Emperor on Horseback Skip to main content Curator Fraser Hunter examines the bronze leg. Duncan McGlynn In 1820, a larger-than-life gilded bronze lower leg was pulled out of a bog in the Scottish Borders region. For more than two centuries, historians discredited the idea that the Roman-era artifact came from Scotland, instead assuming that it was hacked off a monument in England and hauled north by marauding tribes. But ahead of “ Roman Scotland: Life on the Edge of Empire ,” an exhibition at the National Museum of Scotland (NMS), researchers have determined that the so-called “Milsington leg” was not stolen from the south, nor was it violently severed. Instead, they posit that it formed part of a colossal equestrian statue of the Roman Emperor Antoninus Pius that once stood in southern Scotland in the second century C.E., before it was dismantled by retreating Roman troops. “This really turns on its head our understanding of Rome’s second attempt at conquering Scotland,” Fraser Hunter , principal curator of prehistoric and Roman archaeology at NMS, says in a statement . The bronze leg shows no signs of being violently hacked off the larger statue. National Museums Scotland Roman campaigns into modern-day Scotland began in the 70s C.E., several decades after the conquest of Britain . Two subplots using pyplot # A typical pyplot usage pattern is to create subplots incrementally through subplot . The three-digit number passed to subplot specifies the position of the subplot in the grid of subplots. 211 means "in a grid of 2 rows and 1 column, create this subplot in the 1st position". 212 likewise means "in a grid of 2 rows and 1 column, create this subplot in the 2nd position". After calling subplot() all following pyplot commands will modify that subplot until a new subplot is created. import matplotlib.pyplot as plt import numpy as np def f ( t ): return np . exp ( - t ) * np . cos ( 2 * np . pi * t ) t1 = np . arange ( 0.0 , 5.0 , 0.1 ) t2 = np . arange ( 0.0 , 5.0 , 0.02 ) plt . figure () plt . subplot ( 211 ) plt . plot ( t1 , f ( t1 ), color = 'tab:blue' , marker = 'o' ) plt . plot ( t2 , f ( t2 ), color = 'black' ) plt . title ( "Subplot 1" ) plt . subplot ( 212 ) plt . plot ( t2 , np . cos ( 2 * np . pi * t2 ), color = 'tab:orange' , linestyle = '--' ) plt . title ( "Subplot 2" ) plt . show () References The use of the following functions, methods, classes and modules is shown in this example: matplotlib.pyplot.figure matplotlib.pyplot.subplot Download Jupyter notebook: pyplot_two_subplots.ipynb Download Python source code: pyplot_two_subplots.py Download zipped: pyplot_two_subplots.zip

Type 1 Diabetes and Pregnancy May 15, 2024 Español Key points Women with type 1 diabetes can have a healthy pregnancy. Find out how to boost your health before you become pregnant. Have a diabetes management plan, ideally before, during, and after pregnancy, to keep you and your baby healthy. Before you get pregnant Manage your blood sugar Many doctors recommend that you reach and stay at your A1C goal for a few months before becoming pregnant. Review your medicines Some medicines and supplements aren't safe to use while pregnant. Speak with your health care team about each medicine and supplement you take before you get pregnant. Don't stop taking prescribed medicines without talking to your doctor first. During your pregnancy During your pregnancy, you and your doctors will adjust your diabetes management plan. If these health care specialists aren't part of your diabetes care team already, consider looking for: An endocrinologist (a doctor who treats hormone conditions, including diabetes). You may want to find one who specializes in caring for pregnant women with diabetes. An obstetrician (a doctor who treats pregnant women).

People with type 1 diabetes need to take insulin every day. Currently, type 1 diabetes can't be prevented, but it can be treated effectively. What is type 1 diabetes? If you have type 1 diabetes, your pancreas doesn't make insulin or makes very little insulin. Insulin helps blood sugar enter the cells in your body for use as energy. Without insulin, blood sugar can't get into cells and builds up in the bloodstream. High blood sugar is damaging to the body and causes many of the symptoms and complications of diabetes. Type 1 diabetes was once called insulin-dependent or juvenile diabetes. It often develops in children, teens, and young adults, but it can happen at any age. Type 1 diabetes is less common than type 2 —about 5-10% of people with diabetes have type 1. Type 2 Diabetes and Your Liver Sept. 25, 2025 Key points Did you know that type 2 diabetes and overweight can increase your risk for liver disease? Learn more about this connection and how to care for your liver. All about your liver Your liver is the largest internal organ in your body, and it's responsible for many vital functions, including: Filtering your blood to remove wastes like chemicals or toxins. Breaking down medicines and other substances. Producing bile, which helps you digest fat. Helping your immune system fight germs that could make you sick. Your liver also plays a key role in balancing your blood sugar levels. When you eat, a hormone called insulin removes extra sugar from your bloodstream. This sugar is stored in your liver for future use. Between meals and overnight, your liver releases that sugar back into your bloodstream so your body has the energy it needs. There are three types of accounts on GitHub. User accounts Organization accounts Enterprise accounts Every person who uses GitHub signs in to a user account. User accounts Every person who uses GitHub signs in to a user account. Your user account is your identity on GitHub and has a username and profile. For example, see @octocat's profile . Your user account can own resources such as repositories, packages, and projects. Any time you take any action on GitHub, such as creating an issue or reviewing a pull request, the action is attributed to your user account. User accounts are intended for humans, but you can create accounts to automate activity on GitHub. This type of account is called a machine user. Source code: Lib/typing.py Note The Python runtime does not enforce function and variable type annotations. They can be used by third party tools such as type checkers , IDEs, linters, etc. This module provides runtime support for type hints. Consider the function below: def surface_area_of_cube ( edge_length : float ) -> str : return f "The surface area of the cube is { 6 * edge_length ** 2 } ." The function surface_area_of_cube takes an argument expected to be an instance of float , as indicated by the type hint edge_length: float . The function is expected to return an instance of str , as indicated by the -> str hint. While type hints can be simple classes like float or str , they can also be more complex. pages.text: Tyson Fury vs Anthony Joshua: Jai Opetaia pulls out of Deontay Wilder fight - BBC Sport Image source, Getty Images Image caption, Deontay Wilder (left) has won 45 of his 50 fights, while Jai Opetaia has never lost By Kal Sajad BBC Sport boxing journalist Published 18 November 2026 Australian Jai Opetaia has withdrawn from his heavyweight fight with Deontay Wilder on the undercard of Tyson Fury's bout with Anthony Joshua. Unbeaten cruiserweight champion Jai Opetaia was set to step up to heavyweight for the first time to face American Wilder at Cardiff's Principality Stadium on 11 December. Opetaia, 31, did not give a reason for his withdrawal, but it is understood he aggravated a hand injury in training. "Apologies to everyone and especially [Wilder] and his team for withdrawing from the bout," he wrote on Instagram. "Fighter to fighter, I know the feeling and it's frustrating. I've always prided myself on fighting anyone, any place." Opetaia criticised "keyboard warriors" who suggested he was scared off by Wilder's powerful right hand. Opetaia, who has won all 31 of his professional bouts, reiterated his ambition to become undisputed cruiserweight champion. Unified champion David Benavidez has expressed an interest in facing Opetaia in 2027. Britons queuing up to fight Wilder Opetaia's withdrawal leaves a significant gap on the undercard of one of the biggest all-British heavyweight fights in history. pages.text: Türkiye | News | FAO in Türkiye Share Close Türkiye From field evidence to national strategy: Türkiye advances agroecology as a pathway for climate-resilient agrifood systems ©FAO 01/07/2026 Ankara, Türkiye – Türkiye is advancing a national pathway for agroecological transformation, positioning agrifood systems at the centre of climate and sustainability policy. On 14–15 May 2026, FAO and the General Directorate of Agricultural Reform of the Ministry of Agriculture and Forestry of Türkiye organized an Agroecology Workshop in Ankara under the project “Enhancement of agro-ecological management system through promoting ecosystem-oriented food production”, which is being carried out in Bolu province. The workshop brought together representatives from public institutions, academia, international organizations, civil society and technical experts to discuss the scaling up of agroecological food production systems, sustainable natural resource management and the integration of agroecology into policy development and implementation. The workshop also discussed Türkiye’s first national agroecology strategy document , which is now in draft form and was shared with stakeholders. “The draft strategy is timely as Türkiye prepares to host the 31st Conference of the Parties of the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya in November, said Deputy Director General of the General Directorate of Agricultural Reform Abdulkadir Karabulut, in his opening remarks at the workshop. Arlo Parks’s new album Ambiguous Desire is out in April via Transgressive Records. _sullman By Graeme Green Published April 9, 2026 This article was produced by National Geographic Traveller (UK). What’s your earliest travel memory? Going to the south of France. My parents used to drive straight down from London to Nice, sometimes in one 17-hour road trip. We’d listen to my dad’s audiobooks and watch cartoons in the back. I remember spending time in different parts of the south, going through olive trees and to the ocean. I was at my bookworm peak, so I’d always go out to a field or tuck myself away in a corner of the house to read. Do you have a favourite place in the world? São Paulo in Brazil. I loved wandering the streets, getting lost, exploring street markets. I went dancing in clubs with these little local bands of 70-year-old men who’d been playing in jazz outfits since they were 20. They had everyone dancing in the streets, it was really special. I have Brazilian ancestry, so I felt like I was home in a way. United States Attorneys The United States Attorneys are the chief federal law enforcement officers in their districts, responsible for federal criminal prosecutions and civil cases involving the United States Government. The Executive Office for United States Attorneys provides support and oversight for the 94 offices across the country. More information can be found on the United States Attorneys' homepage . Assistant United States Attorneys Assistant United States Attorneys (AUSAs) are responsible for representing the Federal Government in virtually all litigation involving the United States. 28 U.S.C. § 545, requires that all AUSAs reside in the district for which he or she is appointed or within 25 miles thereof. Most United States Attorneys’ Offices are divided into the following sections: Criminal Division Civil Division Appellate Division Financial Litigation Unit Opportunities are posted on our Attorney Job Openings page . Attorney General's Honors Program Each year, several of the United States Attorneys’ offices hire entry-level attorneys through the Attorney General’s Honors Program. If so, a career at a United States Attorney's Office or the Executive Office for United States Attorneys might be for you! Justice for All As the Nation's principal litigators under the direction of the Attorney General, the United States Attorneys conduct most of the trial work in which the United States is a party. The United States Attorneys have three statutory responsibilities: Prosecution of criminal cases brought by the Federal Government; Prosecution and defense of civil cases; and Collection of debts owed the Federal Government which are administratively uncollectible. Careers for All Each of us has something unique and valuable to contribute. Over 12,000 employees enjoy exciting and rewarding careers with the United States Attorneys' offices and the Executive Office for United States Attorneys. We are committed to fostering a diverse and inclusive work environment. pages.text: U.S. Attorneys | Contact Us Skip to main content Contact Us Share Facebook X LinkedIn Email Thank you for visiting the website for the Offices of the United States Attorneys. Please feel free to contact us using the information below. Mail Correspondence to the Executive Office for United States Attorneys may be sent to: Executive Office for United States Attorneys United States Department of Justice 950 Pennsylvania Avenue, NW, Room 2242 Washington, DC 20530-0001 Visit the Find Your United States Attorney page to find a mailing address for your local district office. Phone Department of Justice Main Phone Line - (202) 514-2000 Visit the Find Your United States Attorney page to find a phone number for your local district office. Electronic Message Send a message to the Executive Office for United States Attorneys and district offices. Messages will be forwarded to the responsible Department of Justice component for appropriate handling. If you know the specific organization, district, or official you wish to contact, please indicate such in your message or check the Find Your United States Attorney page to contact them directly.
